text: sync: list-existence oracle (422 unknown_list vs 403 not_a_member) defeats the uniform-403 rule

Done in fe527d5, but NOT the way the ticket first proposed. Collapsing into 403 would have regressed both clients: they quarantine a 422 naming a row_id and hard-fail a 403, so a 403 would wedge the whole push queue behind one unpushable row. Both cases now answer 422 unknown_list + row_id instead - uniform AND quarantine-preserving, and it improves the legitimate case of a device pushing to a list the account has left. The list-level oracle (_apply_list) stays open and is documented in place: pushing an unused id CREATES the list, so free-vs-taken cannot be hidden without server-minted ids, which the offline-first model rules out. Wire contract updated.
